deed: חברת ווייסאיט הישראלית פיתחה אפליקציה שמאפשרת לאנשים עם דיבור לקוי לתקשר בקולם
title: Israel's Voiceitt developed an app that learns impaired speech and turns it into clear speech

trailer.text: Voiceitt is an Israeli company that develops speech recognition technology for atypical speech.
The company was founded in 2012 by Danny Weissberg and Stas Tiomkin, both graduates of the Technion.
Weissberg came up with the idea after his grandmother suffered from a speech impairment following a stroke.
The app learns the user's pronunciation, and after brief training it instantly turns the user's words into clear speech, as audio or text.

In 2021 the company announced the launch of the app on the Apple App Store; it makes it easier for people with non-standard speech to communicate with those around them and to operate devices by voice.

paragraphs.text: Danny Weissberg's grandmother had a stroke, and from then on she struggled to communicate.
Her full-time caregiver gradually learned to understand her speech.
Weissberg said that in the hospital, it was the nurse who cared for his grandmother who was the only one who understood her without difficulty.
According to him, the most painful part was the frustration: his grandmother lost her independence, and the family lost the ability to talk with her.
According to an article on Mako, Weissberg conceived the idea not at the office but following an upsetting family event: his grandmother's stroke, which happened 15 years before the article.
Sara Smolley, who later joined as a co-founder, also has a family story.
Her grandmother was diagnosed with early-onset Parkinson's disease at age 40 and lost much of her motor capabilities.
Voice systems were built for standard speech, and so they leave out millions of people with speech impairments or with a strong accent.
Any atypical speech, such as slurred pronunciation, a heavy accent or an unsupported language, makes using voice assistants difficult.
According to Weissberg, speech-to-text tools are meant for the mass market and the 90 percent of the population that speaks in a standard way.
According to a document of a European project, over one million people around the world suffer from some form of speech disability.

According to ASHA, between 5% and 10% of Americans have some form of communication disorder, and it estimates that these disorders cost the United States approximately $154 billion to $186 billion a year.
According to the same European document, existing augmentative and alternative communication devices are cumbersome, and expensive if high accuracy is wanted.
Discussions with speech therapists revealed that impaired speech affects many children and adults, with a range of conditions.
In 2014 Weissberg said that, to his surprise, no one had a solution like theirs.

stations.title: Two Technion graduates and one idea

paragraphs.text: Since 1999 Weissberg had worked as a software developer at high-tech companies such as Check Point, Radvision and HP, and he saw the potential of the early machine-learning technology of the time to mimic what the caregiver had done naturally.
He also volunteered with the elderly and with the organization Save a Child’s Heart, and saw the idea as an opportunity to make an impact.
Weissberg described the moment of insight: if the human brain can learn to understand people with a speech disability, perhaps an artificial intelligence system can succeed too.
Stas Tiomkin, a speech recognition expert and, like Weissberg, a graduate of the Technion, was then researching machine learning at the Hebrew University.
According to Weissberg, Tiomkin thought the idea was unique and feasible.
According to the company, the two founded Voiceitt in 2012, and Sara Smolley joined a few years later.
When the company had three people, it won two development grants from Israel's Office of the Chief Scientist.
According to a document of a European project, the company developed Talkitt, an app that translates unintelligible sounds into clear speech in real time.
As part of the project, a market validation was planned with organizations and users in Israel, the UK, Italy and Spain.

stations.title: How a machine learns to listen

paragraphs.text: Weissberg said they began developing a speech recognition engine that learns a person's speech the way a person does, and builds a personalized speech model for him.
In 2014 he stressed that the company does pattern recognition, not speech recognition.
He gave an example: a child might say "yum, yum, yum" when he wants to say he is hungry, and a new caregiver does not know this dictionary.
According to TechCrunch, users read short, useful sentences out loud to the app, and it learns their pronunciation.
After brief training it instantly turns their words into clear speech, as audio or as a text message.
According to the company, the engine also recognizes syllables, cadence of speech, breathing pauses and non-verbal sounds, in any language.

stations.title: Hundreds of people tried it, and the app changed

paragraphs.text: In 2017 the company's pilot customers were hospitals and schools, with people whose speech differs because of a health condition.
Weissberg said that in the year before the launch, several hundred people with various speech disabilities tried the app, as a research group.
From the research group they learned that it is important to operate the system with a single button press, to make things easier for people with motor disabilities.
Following the feedback, virtual dividers were added that divide the word bank by different situations in life.

stations.title: Turning on the light by voice: the connection to Alexa

paragraphs.text: According to The Spoon, without voice control people with cerebral palsy depend on caregivers even to turn on a light.
Weissberg said that for a person with motor and speech limitations, who cannot turn on a light or change a channel, Alexa can be life-changing.
In 2018 Voiceitt took part in the Alexa Accelerator in Seattle, and received investment from Amazon through the Alexa Fund.
A person who cannot use Alexa because of a speech disability can speak to Voiceitt, and it translates what he says and passes it to Alexa.
Peter Korn, an accessibility director at Amazon Lab126, said that in collaboration with Voiceitt they were able to bring Alexa to more customers.
At ALYN Hospital in Jerusalem, one of the company's Israeli testing sites, Voiceitt was adopted so that patients could speak with Alexa in Hebrew or Arabic.

stations.title: The launch, and what came after

paragraphs.text: On June 8, 2021, Voiceitt announced the launch of its app on the Apple App Store.
At launch, the app was offered for free for a limited period.
According to the company, isolation and social distancing during the coronavirus period cut off many people with speech and motor impairments from their loved ones.

According to Mako, Voiceitt launched the world's first app that offers a solution to the problem of people whose voices speech recognition systems, even the most advanced ones, cannot recognize and decipher because of a condition such as a stroke or cerebral palsy.
"Everyone deserves to be able to express themselves and to be understood," Weissberg said at the launch.
The company won Microsoft's AI For Good competition and received a grant from its AI for Accessibility Fund.
According to G3ict, it won a Best of Innovation award in the accessibility category at CES 2021.
In 2017 it was reported that it had raised $2 million in seed funding.
In 2023 Voiceitt 2 was released, a web app that lets people with speech disabilities speak spontaneously and be understood.
The company's CEO, Allison Pace, said it was a milestone in the evolution of the technology and the business.
According to CNN, the company also developed integrations with WebEx and ChatGPT and a Chrome extension that turns non-standard speech into captions on the screen.
Colin Hughes, a former BBC producer who uses the app, said it is impressively accurate with his atypical speech, and that the training and setup are straightforward.
Sara Smolley said that Voiceitt is to today's remote workplace what a ramp once was to an office building.
According to G3ict, the company's partner network includes healthcare providers, therapists and researchers in the US, Israel and Europe.
According to a 2023 article, the company expected to expand to the UK and Australia by 2024.
Colin Hughes, who praises the app, has also criticized it.
According to him, Voiceitt is best suited to single-sentence messages, and he calls for adding features such as voice-driven cursor control and better dictation of long texts.
CNN noted that technology that captures and stores private voice recordings may concern users.
According to CNN, Apple also launched in 2024 a feature called Listen for Atypical Speech, which recognizes a wider range of speech patterns.

versions.says: ISRAEL21c article from 2014: in Ramat Gan
Company announcement from 2021: in Tel Aviv, with a subsidiary in the United States

disagreements.question: How much money did the company raise?

versions.says: ISRAEL21c in 2021: $17 million, from investors such as Amazon's Alexa Fund and Microsoft's M12
The Spoon: $16 million, including non-equity money from governments and funds
MobiHealthNews: $10 million in the summer before the article, to support people with speech impairments during the coronavirus.

disagreements.question: How much does using the app cost?

versions.says: The Spoon: a subscription of $200 a year in the U.S.
Article from 2014: the company was working on a subscription of about $20 per month
CNN in 2024: a per-minute or per-user license, at prices from $20 to $50

disagreements.question: Which pilot led to the connection with Alexa?

versions.says: ISRAEL21c: a pilot with AARP, together with an investment from AARP
G3ict: a successful pilot with Inglis House in Philadelphia, a community for people with physical disabilities

claims.text: בית החולים אלי"ן בירושלים, אתר ניסוי ישראלי של החברה, אימץ את Voiceitt כדי שמטופלים ישוחחו עם אלקסה בעברית או בערבית.
claims.quote: One of the company’s Israeli testing sites, ALYN Pediatric and Adolescent Rehabilitation Hospital in Jerusalem, adopted Voiceitt to allow patients with atypical speech to interact with Alexa in Hebrew or Arabic.

claims.text: האפליקציה ניתנה בחינם בהשקה לתקופה מוגבלת.
claims.quote: The assistive technology app, which will be offered for free at launch for a limited period, empowers individuals to navigate their environments

claims.text: לפי החברה, הבידוד והריחוק החברתי בעקבות הקורונה הותירו אנשים רבים עם לקויות דיבור ותנועה מנותקים מיקיריהם.
claims.quote: Isolation and social distancing in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic have left many individuals with speech and motor impairments either separated from loved ones

claims.text: לפי מאקו, החברה השיקה את האפליקציה הראשונה בעולם שמציעה פתרון לבעיה זו.
claims.quote: השיקה את האפליקציה הראשונה בעולם שמציעה פתרון לבעיה הזו

claims.text: וייסברג אמר בהשקה שכל אחד ראוי שיוכל להביע את עצמו ושיבינו אותו.
claims.quote: Everyone deserves to be able to express themselves and to be understood

claims.text: Voiceitt זכתה בתחרות AI For Good של מיקרוסופט וקיבלה מענק מקרן AI for Accessibility שלה.
claims.quote: Voiceitt won Microsoft’s AI For Good competition and received a grant from its AI for Accessibility Fund.

claims.text: ב-2017 דווח שהחברה גייסה 2 מיליון דולר במימון זרע.
claims.quote: a Tel Aviv-based startup called Voiceitt has raised $2 million in seed funding to translate into clear words speech that’s not easily intelligible

claims.text: Voiceitt 2 היא אפליקציית ווב חדשה שמאפשרת לאנשים עם מוגבלות דיבור לדבר באופן ספונטני ולהיות מובנים.
claims.quote: Voiceitt 2, developed by Voiceitt, lets people with speech disabilities speak spontaneously and be understood by others.

claims.text: בשנת 2023 אליסון פייס, מנכ"לית Voiceitt, אמרה ששחרור Voiceitt2 הוא אבן דרך בהתפתחות הטכנולוגיה והעסק.
claims.quote: The launch of Voiceitt2 is an important milestone in the evolution of Voiceitt’s technology and business

claims.text: לפי CNN, Voiceitt פיתחה שילובים עם WebEx ו-ChatGPT ותוסף לכרום שהופכים דיבור לא סטנדרטי לכתוביות על המסך.
claims.quote: Voiceitt has developed integrations with WebEx and ChatGPT, along with a Google Chrome extension, which convert non-standard speech to captions shown on the screen.

claims.text: קולין יוז, מפיק לשעבר ב-BBC ומשתמש באפליקציה, אמר שהיא מדויקת להפליא עם דיבורו הלא טיפוסי ושהאימון וההגדרה פשוטים.
claims.quote: I found Voiceitt’s app to be impressively accurate with my atypical speech, and its training and setup process was straightforward

claims.text: סמולי אמרה ש-Voiceitt היא למקום העבודה המרוחק של היום מה שהייתה רמפה לבניין משרדים בעבר.
claims.quote: What a (wheelchair) ramp was to yesterday’s office building Voiceitt is to today’s remote workplace

claims.text: לפי G3ict, רשת השותפים של Voiceitt כוללת ספקי שירותי בריאות, מטפלים וחוקרים בארה"ב, בישראל ובאירופה.
claims.quote: Voiceitt’s network of international partners also includes healthcare providers, speech and occupational therapists, researchers, and disability organizations in the US, Israel, and throughout Europe

claims.text: לפי הכתבה מ-2023, החברה מרמת גן צפתה להתרחב לבריטניה ולאוסטרליה עד 2024.
claims.quote: The Ramat Gan-based company expects to expand to the UK and Australia by 2024

claims.text: יוז ביקר: לדבריו Voiceitt מתאימה ביותר להודעות של משפט אחד, והוא קורא לתכונות כמו שליטה בסמן בקול ושיפור הכתבה לטקסטים ארוכים.
claims.quote: He advocates for features like voice-driven cursor control and improved dictation recognition for drafting long-form content, saying that Voiceitt works best for single-sentence messages.

claims.text: CNN ציינה שבטכנולוגיה שאוספת ושומרת הקלטות קול פרטיות עלולה להיות סיבת דאגה למשתמשים.
claims.quote: With technology that captures and stores personal data such as voice recordings, privacy can be a concern for users.

claims.text: לפי CNN, אפל השיקה בתחילת השנה את התכונה Listen for Atypical Speech שמזהה מגוון רחב יותר של דפוסי דיבור.
claims.quote: Earlier this year, Apple (AAPL) launched its AI-powered “Listen for Atypical Speech” feature, which uses machine learning to recognize a wider range of speech patterns.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c ב-2021, Voiceitt גייסה 17 מיליון דולר ממשקיעים כמו קרן אלקסה של אמזון ו-M12 של מיקרוסופט.
claims.quote: Voiceitt has raised $17 million from Amazon Alexa Fund, M12 (Microsoft’s venture capital fund), AMIT Technion, Viking Maccabee Ventures

claims.text: לפי The Spoon, Voiceitt גייסה 16 מיליון דולר, כולל כסף שאינו הון מממשלות וקרנות אחרות.
claims.quote: Voiceitt has raised $16 million in funding so far including non-equity money from governments and other funds

claims.text: לפי MobiHealthNews, Voiceitt גייסה 10 מיליון דולר בקיץ הקודם כדי לתמוך באנשים עם לקויות דיבור בזמן מגפת הקורונה.
claims.quote: Voiceitt raised $10 million last summer to support people with speech impairments during the COVID-19 pandemic.

claims.text: לפי The Spoon, האפליקציה תהיה זמינה בארה"ב בסוף מאי במנוי של 200 דולר בשנה.
claims.quote: The Voiceitt app will be available here in the U.S. at the end of May, with a subscription of $200 a year

claims.text: בכתבה מ-2014 נמסר שהחברה עובדת על מודל מנוי של כ-20 דולר לחודש.
claims.quote: For now, VoiceITT is working on a subscription model of about $20 per month.

claims.text: לפי CNN ב-2024, התוכנה נמכרת ברישיון לדקה או למשתמש במחירים של 20 עד 50 דולר.
claims.quote: The software is sold as either a per-minute or per-user license, with prices ranging from $20 to $50.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, פיילוט עם AARP, יחד עם השקעה של AARP, הוביל לשילוב ממשק Alexa באפליקציה.
claims.quote: A pilot in collaboration with the American Association of Retired Persons (AARP) followed along with investment from AARP.

claims.text: לפי G3ict, השותפות עם אלקסה באה בעקבות פיילוט מוצלח עם Inglis House בפילדלפיה, קהילה לאנשים עם מוגבלות פיזית.
claims.quote: The partnership with Alexa followed a successful pilot with Inglis House, a long-term care wheelchair community for people with physical disabilities based in Philadelphia.

claims.text: לפי כתבה במאקו, וייסברג לא הגה את הרעיון במשרד אלא בעקבות אירוע משפחתי מטלטל: השבץ של סבתו, שאירע 15 שנים לפני הכתבה.
claims.quote: בעקבות אירוע מטלטל שחווה לפני 15 שנים
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page

claims.text: וייסברג עבד מאז 1999 כמפתח תוכנה בחברות הייטק כמו צ'ק פוינט, רדוויז'ן ו-HP, וזיהה פוטנציאל בטכנולוגיית למידת המכונה המוקדמת של אותם ימים, שתוכל לחקות את מה שהמטפלת עשתה באופן טבעי.
claims.quote: Weissberg spotted the potential of early machine-learning technology to mimic what the caregiver had done naturally.
